newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks drift lower in seesaw activity.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks drift lower in seesaw activity.

text.p: ** (1330 GMT) - Indian shares finish with modest losses in
choppy trade, local funds among major sellers
** Bombay share index ends 25.77 points, or 0.63 pct down
** India's central bank cuts interest rates by one
percentage point to 10 percent, move seen helping stocks
** Reliance ends 8.0 rupees lower at 366.50 ahead of
bonus share announcement due on Thursday
** National exchange index gains 4.75 pts at 1,160.05
** Delhi shr index down 1.07 pts at 866.23, Calcutta eases
0.77 pts at 119.56 and Madras 26.85 pts at 4,275.71
Indian shares finished broadly lower in a roller-coaster ride on Wednesday, with local funds booking profits from a recent rally, traders said.
However, strong buying support seen at lower levels was indicative of a firm market undertone, they said.
A one percentage point reduction in interest rates by the central bank announced after the close of market could help firm sentiment on Thursday, traders said.
"It is very positive for the markets," said Ramnath Iyer, strategist at Peregrine Capital India. "It was completely unexpected as there is already a lot of liquidity."
Market participants said today's fall in prices was a correction, with the focus continuing on leading private firm Reliance Industries ahead of its Thursday bonus announcement.

"All the good news will come tomorrow," said an analyst at a leading U.S. investment bank. "We expect Reliance to announce a generous bonus ratio and talk about a jump in sales and profit in the current financial year."

Reliance lost 8.0 rupees at 366.50 with 11 million shares traded. Chairman Dhirubhai Ambani is due to address shareholders at the firm's annual meeting on Thursday just after the board of directors meets to finalise the bonus issue.
